Definition: a lattice; (by implication) a window, dovecot (because of the pigeon-holes), chimney (with its apertures for smoke), sluice (with openings for water)
BiblicalUsage: The window is the lattice in the sky, and Scripture opens it for flood and for blessing alike. In the days of Noah the windows of heaven were opened, a lord of Samaria scoffs that even if the LORD should make windows in heaven such a thing could not be, and Malachi promises that God will open the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing there is not room enough to receive.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the windows of heaven say the same thing in judgment and in blessing: heaven is not shut. It opens to flood the earth, and it opens to feed the hungry, and I hold that the God who opens the windows is the same God in both, and His opening is always according to His word.
